title: What a water project really costs

blocks.text: A water utility's planners keep asking two questions about their project list before any model is solved. Each project has a cost (in $k) and a tuple of `needs`: the projects that must also be funded for it to go ahead. A needed project may have needs of its own, and two projects may need the same one.

items: "What does it take to fund this project?" `entry_cost(projects, pid)` returns the cost of `pid` plus the cost of every project it needs, directly or through other needed projects. A project that is needed along two paths is still built, and paid for, once.

"Which projects are required only because something required needs them?" `implied_required(projects, required)` returns the set of projects that are not in `required` but that some project in `required` needs, directly or indirectly.

blocks.text: `projects` maps each id to a `Project`. No project needs itself, directly or indirectly.

Write both functions in `entry.py`. Draw the needs of the test instances as a graph first (an arrow from each project to each project it needs), and decide what a walk over that graph must remember. About fifteen lines.

cases.says: a project that needs nothing costs its own cost
a project's entry cost adds the cost of the project it needs
a required project's prerequisite is reported as required too
a prerequisite's own prerequisites are paid for and required too
a prerequisite reached through two paths is paid for once

origin.section: Read the Dependency Graph Before You Solve

concepts: the parent graph shows implied must-dos, children that can never start, and cycles before any solve
